<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Terrorism in Pakistan]]
**[[Pakistan]]i authorities announce they have arrested five suspected members of [[al-Qaeda]] in the eastern province of [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]], as they are reported to have been planning an attack on security personnel. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-arrests/pakistan-seizes-five-suspected-al-qaeda-militants-idUSKBN1YV10I?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Iraqi insurgency (2017–present)]]
**A rocket attack on [[K-1 Air Base]] in [[Iraq]]'s [[Kirkuk Governorate]], kills an [[Americans|American]] civilian contractor and injures several [[United States Army|U.S.]] and [[Iraqi Army|Iraqi]] troops. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/us-civilian-contractor-killed-troops-injured-rocket-attack/story?id=67949811 (ABC News)]

;Arts and culture
*The [[Government of the Netherlands|Dutch government]] announces it will officially stop using the moniker "[[Holland]]" from January 2020, so the country will only be referred to by its official name, the Netherlands. The change comes ahead of the [[2020 Summer Olympics]] and [[Eurovision Song Contest 2020]], which the country is due to participate in. [https://www.independent.co.uk/travel/news-and-advice/netherlands-holland-dutch-tourism-board-logo-a9261266.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[2018 Moscow–Constantinople schism]]
**The [[Russian Orthodox Church]] cuts ties with the [[Greek Orthodox Church of Alexandria]] over the former's recognition of the [[Orthodox Church of Ukraine]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2019/12/27/world/europe/ap-eu-russia-orthodox-church-africa.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Business and economics
*[[Spotify]] announces it will suspend all political ads on its platform starting early 2020. It follows similar moves from [[Twitter]] and [[Google]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-spotify-political-ads/spotify-to-suspend-political-advertising-in-2020-idUSKBN1YV1GI (Reuters)]
*[[Sudan]]ese Finance Minister Ibrahim Elbadawi states that, as part of the [[Government of Sudan|government]] budget for 2020, subsidies for [[gasoline]] will be gradually lifted while the [[minimum wage]] and pay for [[civil servant]]s will increase in an effort to combat both [[inflation]] and poverty. The budget, which will be finalized in two days, will also increase spending on [[Education in Sudan|education]], social services, and aid to [[Refugees of Sudan#Internally displaced Sudanese|refugees]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sudan-economy/sudan-to-lift-fuel-subsidies-gradually-in-2020-minister-idUSKBN1YV1LY?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Bek Air Flight 2100]]
**A [[Fokker 100]] plane with 98 people on board crashes while taking off from [[Almaty International Airport]], [[Kazakhstan]], killing 12 and injuring about 60 others. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-50922219 (BBC News)]
*A sightseeing helicopter crashes on the [[Hawaii|Hawaiian]] island of [[Kauai, Hawaii|Kauai]], killing seven people on board. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-50927645 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*The [[Food and Drug Administration]] announces that [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] signed legislation last week to amend the [[Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act]] which will raise the [[smoking age|legal age to buy tobacco]] in the U.S. from 18 to 21 in the next three to six months. [https://www.abc12.com/content/news/566498521.html (Gray News)]

;International relations
*[[Iran–Japan relations]]
**After briefing the [[Iranian government]], the [[Cabinet of Japan]] approves the deployment of a [[destroyer]] and patrol planes to the [[Middle East]] (independent from similar [[United States Armed Forces|U.S.]]-led and [[European Union|European]] missions) to protect [[Japan Self-Defense Forces|Japanese]] vessels, as the situation in the region remains volatile. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-iran-japan/japan-to-send-warship-aircraft-to-middle-east-to-protect-vessels-idUSKBN1YV00W (Reuters)]
*[[Chagos Archipelago sovereignty dispute]]
**[[Prime Minister of Mauritius|Mauritian Prime Minister]] [[Pravind Jugnauth]] says he is considering bringing charges of [[crimes against humanity]] against [[United Kingdom|British]] officials in the [[International Criminal Court]] (ICC) over the UK's refusal to allow [[Expulsion of the Chagossians|evicted]] [[Chagossians]] to return to their former homes on the [[Chagos Archipelago]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-50924704 (BBC News)]
*[[Philippines–United States relations]]
**[[Philippines|Philippine]] [[President of the Philippines|President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] bans [[United States Senate|U.S. Senators]] [[Dick Durbin]] and [[Patrick Leahy]] from entering the country, as both are seeking to enforce sanctions on politicians involved in the prosecution of [[Senator of the Philippines|Philippine Senator]] and [[Presidency of Rodrigo Duterte|Duterte administration]] critic [[Leila de Lima]]. Duterte also threatens to tighten [[Visa policy of the Philippines|visa requirements]] for American citizens should the sanctions go through. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-philippines-usa-duterte/philippines-bans-two-u-s-senators-mulls-new-visa-rules-for-americans-idUSKBN1YV0GX (Reuters)]

;Science and technology
*[[Russia]]'s [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Ministry of Defence]] announces the first deployment of the [[Avangard (hypersonic glide vehicle)|Avangard]] [[Boost-glide|hypersonic glide vehicle]] (HGV), calling it a "landmark event". According to President [[Vladimir Putin]], the top speed is over [[Mach number|Mach]] 20 and it puts Russia's military "ahead of all other nations". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-50927648 (BBC News)]
